**6B.5 Research Note**

**Verdict:** mostly no. I found some real signs of administrative correction in social-service delivery, especially in rural healthcare staffing and disability/family benefits. But I did not find strong evidence of a broader culture of measurement, independent evaluation, or transparent correction. The dominant pattern is still top-down control, secrecy, and patronage.

| Stance | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | [Government increased special social payments for medical workers](https://government.ru/news/51150/) | Government of Russia | 2024-03-21 | https://government.ru/news/51150/ | Putin ordered higher monthly payments for medical workers in rural areas, district centers, and small towns, explicitly to support staffing in primary care. This is evidence of responding to service-delivery shortage data, though the report is self-reported. | 6B.5; 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Improving healthcare services for rural areas](https://government.ru/en/news/51246/) | Government of Russia | 2024-03-26 | https://government.ru/en/news/51246/ | The government said it was raising medics’ pay supplements again and extending `Country Doctor` and `Country Paramedic` to attract specialists and improve quality. That is a corrective staffing response, but still official-internal rather than independently audited. | 6B.5; 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Additional financing for rural healthcare workers](https://government.ru/docs/53769/) | Government of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://government.ru/docs/53769/ | The state extended `Zemsky Doctor` and `Zemsky Paramedic` through 2030, raised compensation, allowed one transfer within the region, and said the program brought about 2,000 specialists in 2024. This is the clearest evidence of adaptive correction based on staffing needs. | 6B.5; 6B.4; 6B.2 |
| Support | [Social Fund operations in the new regions in 2024](https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536) | Social Fund of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2024/12/18/276536 | The Social Fund reported digitized sick-leave processing and broader benefit administration in occupied/new regions, including pensions, child benefits, disability support, and health-worker payments. This shows administrative rollout and some service modernization. | 6B.5; 6B.4; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Support | [Rehabilitation support for children with disabilities expanded](https://government.ru/docs/53649/) | Government of Russia | 2024-12-09 | https://government.ru/docs/53649/ | The rehab pilot expanded from 3 to 38 regions and included rehab, lodging, meals, and travel costs. That is a concrete service-delivery adjustment, but the evidence is programmatic expansion, not transparent evaluation. | 6B.5; 6B.2; 6B.3 |
| Support | [AI strategy amendment](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50326/print) | Kremlin | 2024-02-15 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50326/print | The amended AI strategy required state-linked firms to update plans, expand datasets, support open AI libraries, and train civil servants. This is real capacity-building, but only a weak proxy for evidence-based service correction. | 6B.5 |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the system is a kleptocracy with closed decision-making, weak accountability, and loyalty-based distribution of contracts and protection. That is strong evidence against transparent correction. | 6B.5 |
| Against | [Russia: Nations in Transit 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House says regional autonomy was stripped out and policy space controlled from above, which cuts against decentralised measurement and local service-learning. | 6B.5 |
| Against | [Putin widened secrecy privileges for major firms](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001) | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Wider secrecy made it harder for outsiders to judge conditions honestly, weakening the information environment needed for evidence-based correction. | 6B.5 |
| Against | [Russia’s economy shows solid growth despite sanctions](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reuters said growth and low unemployment were heavily driven by military production, not civilian welfare delivery. This weakens the claim that the state was using service metrics to improve ordinary public services. | 6B.5; 6B.2; 6B.4 |
| Against | [War costs forcing tax rises and cuts in education support](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3922326-russia-prepares-for-further-tax-rises-due-to-war-reuters.html) | Ukrinform / Reuters | 2024-11-02 | https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3922326-russia-prepares-for-further-tax-rises-due-to-war-reuters.html | Reuters’ reporting said war costs were forcing tax rises and cuts in other priorities, including small business support and education development. That points to crowding out, not service-learning correction. | 6B.5; 6B.2 |
| Against | [Russia: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | The report says daily government decisions are taken by a small closed circle with little transparency or accountability. That is the opposite of open measurement and correction. | 6B.5 |

**Search gap:** I found some official program revisions and staffing fixes, but almost no evidence of public KPIs, independent service audits, published evaluations, or transparent “we measured X, found failure, and corrected Y” style governance. The strongest positive items are mostly official self-reporting, so they show adjustment more than verifiable evidence-based correction.
